chunks: The first group: That the most detested of creatures to Allah, the Exalted, are two men

One is he whom Allah left to his own self, so he deviates from the straight path, is engrossed in the speech of innovation and the call to misguidance; he is a trial for whoever is tempted by him, astray from the guidance of those who preceded him, misleading whoever follows him in his life and after his death, carrying the sins of others, held captive by his own misdeeds.

key_terms.وَكَلَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَى نَفْسِهِ: He whom Allah left to his own self (self-reliant in a negative sense)

ai.seo_question: Who are the two most detested creatures to Allah according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali identifies this first type as the self-reliant innovator whose deviation causes widespread fitnah, misleading both contemporaries and future generations. This figure is described as carrying the sins of his followers while remaining captive to his own errors, highlighting the spiritual danger of unguided leadership. The description underscores the Shia emphasis on divine guidance over individual caprice in matters of religious authority.
